marks.gloss_en: ומי סבר ליה כוותיה? והא מיפלג פליג עילויה, דתניא: רבי יהודה אומר מעלין את המדומע באחד ומאה; רבי שמעון בן אלעזר אומר נותן עיניו בצד זה ואוכל מצד אחר
R' Yehuda's [view] goes further than R' Shimon ben Elazar's
a stone on the mouth of a barrel: he tilts [the barrel] on its side and it falls
coins on a cushion: he shakes the cushion and they fall
R' Oshaya: one who forgot a purse in the courtyard places a loaf or a baby on it and moves it
טעמא דחזי לאומצא, הא לא חזי לאומצא -- לא. למימרא דרבא כרבי יהודה סבירא ליה? -- the reason is that it is fit raw; were it not, no
Rava holds like R' Yehuda
כמה חריפן שמעתתא דדרדקי! אימר דאמור רבנן בשוכח, לכתחילה מי אמור?! -- the device was permitted for one who forgot, not to be set up deliberately
אימר דאמור רבנן בשוכח, לכתחילה מי אמור?! -- the same rebuke, against Rava's knife on the dove
Abaye would put a spoon on bundles

אי לאו דאדם חשוב אנא, כפא אכיפי למה לי? הא חזו למיזגא עלייהו -- the bundles are themselves fit to lean on; the spoon is only because I am an important person (= p_abaye_adam_chashuv, p_kifei_chazu_lemizga)
Abaye: were I not an important person, why would I need a spoon on the bundles?

אנא, אי לאו דאדם חשוב אנא -- סכינא אבר יונה למה לי? הא חזי לי לאומצא -- the dove is itself fit for me raw; the knife is only because I am an important person (= p_rava_adam_chashuv, p_bar_yona_chazi_leumtza)
Rava: were I not an important person, why would I need a knife on a young dove?
והאמר רבא לשמעיה: טווי לי בר אווזא ושדי מיעיה לשונרא -- Rava himself had the innards thrown to the cat
Rava to his attendant: roast me a duck, and throw its innards to the cat
Mar Zutra: the halakha follows all these teachings, in the case of one who forgets
they taught this only of one who forgot [the stone there]
the mishna, cited as lemma: coins on a cushion -- he shakes the cushion and they fall
they taught [shaking the cushion] only [where he moves it] for the sake of [the cushion] itself
R' Yosei: if the barrel was lying in a storeroom, or glass vessels were lying beneath it -- he lifts it to another place, tilts it on its side, and [the stone] falls
דתנן: הבורר קטנית ביום טוב -- the Beit Shammai / Beit Hillel dispute that RSBG's baraita then qualifies
R' Yochanan: it is Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
ותניא, RSBG: where the waste exceeds the food, all agree he selects the food
RSBG: when is this [dispute] said? where the food exceeds the waste
והא הכא דכי אוכל מרובה על הפסולת דמי! -- but here [the barrel] is like food exceeding the waste
here too, since the wine cannot be taken until he takes the stone, it is like waste exceeding the food
here too, since if he wants to take [it], the wine is not taken until he takes the stone -- it is like waste exceeding the food

wherever there is a prohibited and a permitted item, we exert ourselves with the permitted and do not exert ourselves with the prohibited (presupposed by the stam's מאן תנא on the mishna's 'if it was among the barrels')
